key_insight: PWLNet makes neural process surrogates easier to optimize by combining compact networks with exact or piecewise-linear formulations.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can embed learned steady-state and dynamic process models in Pyomo optimization while balancing predictive accuracy, solve time, and constraint fidelity.
method: Train baseline or physics-informed surrogates with optimization-aware pruning.
Embed ReLU, exact tanh, or PWL-tanh models using MILP, nonlinear optimization, or binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP.
Use PWL-native training to match training and embedding activations without extra linearization error.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks, reported results include a 6.5-fold MILP speedup after 15% pruning on Williams–Otto and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy on Van de Vusse.
watch_item: Constraint fidelity remains a concern: the hydroformylation exact-tanh controller reached 20.002 bar against a 20-bar limit, and longer horizons or physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results.
paper_title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
